name: Facet
text: Choose a single high-contrast dark theme with adjustable saturation and font size. This maximizes visibility and liveliness for our screen-based work while keeping the interface clean and enjoyable. Trade-off: we lose the flexibility of a light theme, but dark themes reduce eye strain in low-light environments, which aligns with our goal of speed and clarity.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A single high-contrast dark theme locks out users who need *low* contrast for readability—no system-preference toggle means we fail accessibility standards outright. Better: a *user-selectable* dark/light toggle with a *third* "auto" mode tied to system preference, but only if we test it with real users to confirm it doesn’t fragment the interface’s speed or clarity. Settle it with a 10-person usability test comparing all three modes on task completion time and error rates.
